definition: דָּת noun feminine Esth 3:15 decree, law , usage, only in Persian period (Biblical Aramaic Late Hebrew id. , Syriac or ; Persian loan-word, Old Persian dâta , law , Spieg APK 225 ) — ׳ ד absolute Esth 1:8 + 9 t.; construct דַּת Esth 2:12 , דָּת Esth 9:13 suffix דָּתוֺ Esth 2:8 + 4 t.; plural construct דָּתֵי Ezra 8:36 + 2 t.; suffix דָּתַיהֶם Esth 3:8 — 1. decree, edict, commission of Persian king Ezra 8:36 (word elsewhere only in Esther) Esth 2:8 (|| דְּבַר הַמֶּלֶךְ ), Esth 4:3 (|| id. ) Esth 8:17 (|| id. ) Esth 9:1 (|| id. ; with עשׂה execute ) compare also Esth 9:13 with verb נָתַן Esth 3:14 ; Esth 3:15 ; Esth 8:13 ; Esth 8:14 ; Esth 9:14 written כְּתָבהַֿדָּת Esth 4:8 (compare Esth 3:14 ; Esth 8:13 ). 2. law , permanently valid and applicable, וְיִכָּתֵב בְּדָתֵי פָּרַסוּֿמָדַי וְלֹא יַעֲבוֺר Esth 1:19 compare v Esth 1:15 ; Esth 4:11 ; Esth 4:16 יֹדְעֵי דָּת וָדִין Esth 1:13 those that understood law and judgment ; דָּתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ Esth 3:8 of laws of the Jews in Persia Esth 3:8 even of rules for drinking at a feast Esth 1:8 for purifying of women Esth 2:12 . — The distinction between 1 & 2 is not absolute . The king's will was law, and the royal edict ( דְּבַר מַלְכוּת ) concerning Vashti was reckoned among the laws ( דָּתֵי ) of the Persians & Medes ( Esth 1:19 ). — In Deut 33:2 ᵑ0 אֵשׁ דָּת לָמוֺ fire was a law for them is corrupt; many emendations proposed, compare Di ; Di suggests דֹת [ לַפִּ ] אֵשׁ fire of flames , flaming fire, compare הַלַּפִּידִם Exod 20:18 (but לַפִּדֹת plural in תֹ֯ not in OT unless as proper name), or (better), דֶת [ יֹקֶ ] אֵשׁ a burning fire , compare Isa 65:5 (different sense).
